summary: Mostly sound Modern Standard Arabic in a professional register, but pf.summary is broken (a stray Chinese character '反', a non-word 'محبز', a changed meaning for 'independently-tested', and no verbatim 'Constitution'). 'Portfolio' was rendered as 'المحفظة' (wallet), 'Work' as 'العمل' (employment), and the 'Primary' nav landmark as 'الرئيسية' (which Arabic users read as 'Home'). The footer leaves 'Belgrade · Dubna' in English, and the desc.fallback attaches 'product' to the wrong placeholder.

checks.meaning_idiom_register: MSA professional-neutral register throughout. Real meaning defects: المحفظة (wallet) for portfolio, العمل (job) for Work, الحداثة (modernity) for novelty, التراث (folklore) for heritage tier, a literal 'itch to scratch' calque, and 'fleet' rendered as أسطول. pf.summary is mistranslated in three places.
checks.script: There is one real defect: U+53CD '反' (CJK) inside pf.summary. Apart from that every string is in Arabic script, with harakat (shadda, damma) used sparingly and correctly. There is no Persian ی/ک contamination.
checks.rtl: With page-level dir=rtl, the strings that start with a Latin run ('%s — ...', footer.text 'Belgrade · Dubna.') resolve correctly, because the paragraph direction is set by dir and not inferred. The '—' between Latin and Arabic runs takes the paragraph direction, so it is safe. The 'footer.version' colon is the plain ':' (Arabic has no separate colon glyph), and the LTR 'v2.0.0' link that follows renders on the left of the colon as expected, so no RLM/LRM is needed. In prod.desc.fallback the two %s stay in source order. Under RTL they display right-to-left (name on the right), which is the correct Arabic reading order. If both values are Latin and are adjacent through '—', they may be visually reordered: the proposed form keeps Arabic 'منتج' between them, which anchors the order. tier.* slugs with hyphens display as isolated LTR runs, which is OK.
checks.plural: No string carries a count or plural form. If counts are ever added (e.g. 'N products'), Arabic needs the full CLDR set: zero/one/two (dual)/few/many/other.
checks.date_number: There are no dates. The only numerals are the tier ordinals 1/2/3 in Western digits, which is acceptable for a tech site (Maghreb and most web UIs use Western digits). Using Arabic-Indic ١/٢/٣ would be a site-wide policy decision, not a defect here.
checks.glossary: Brand and product names are kept Latin. Real violations: 'Constitution' (pf.summary), 'AI' (kw.vasic) and 'Miloš Vasić' (alt.portrait). Fixes keep the Arabic term and add the protected term verbatim where natural.
checks.footer_length: mv footer.text is about 66 characters in English and about 55 in the proposed Arabic. It exceeds about 45 characters, but it is shorter than its source, so it is not a regression. footer.suffix (about 23) and footer.version (about 13) are fine.
